/-!
# Conjecture 1.87

by A. L. Shmel'kin

Problem 1.86 of the Kourovka Notebook (also by Shmel'kin) asks: does every finitely
generated soluble group have a finite basis of identities? Problem 1.87 asks
"the same question for matrix groups (at least over a field of characteristic $0$)":
does every finitely generated group of matrices over a field $K$, i.e. every finitely
generated subgroup of $\mathrm{GL}_n(K)$, have a finite basis of identities? The
proposer asks this at least when $K$ has characteristic $0$.

An identity (law) of a group $G$ is a word $w$ in the free group $F$ on countably many
variables $x_0, x_1, \dots$ such that $w$ evaluates to $1$ under every substitution of
elements of $G$ for the variables, i.e. $\varphi(w) = 1$ for every homomorphism
$\varphi \colon F \to G$. A word $w$ is a consequence of a set $S$ of words if $w$ lies
in the verbal subgroup of $F$ determined by $S$, that is, the subgroup of $F$ generated
by all images of elements of $S$ under endomorphisms of $F$ (the smallest fully
invariant subgroup of $F$ containing $S$). A finite basis of identities of $G$ is a
finite set $S$ of words whose consequences are exactly the identities of $G$;
equivalently, the variety of groups generated by $G$ is finitely based.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

blocks.code:
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem mem_laws_iff {G : Type*} [Group G] {w : FreeGroup ℕ} :
    w ∈ laws G ↔ ∀ f : ℕ → G, FreeGroup.lift f w = 1 := by
  simp only [laws, Subgroup.mem_iInf, MonoidHom.mem_ker]
  exact ⟨fun h f => h (FreeGroup.lift f),
    fun h φ => by simpa using h (FreeGroup.lift.symm φ)⟩
blocks.docstring:
A word `w` is a law of `G` if and only if it evaluates to `1` under every substitution
`f : ℕ → G` of elements of `G` for the variables.

@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem mem_laws_iff {G : Type*} [Group G] {w : FreeGroup ℕ} :
    w ∈ laws G ↔ ∀ f : ℕ → G, FreeGroup.lift f w = 1 := by
  simp only [laws, Subgroup.mem_iInf, MonoidHom.mem_ker]
  exact ⟨fun h f => h (FreeGroup.lift f),
    fun h φ => by simpa using h (FreeGroup.lift.symm φ)⟩

def verbalSubgroup (S : Set (FreeGroup ℕ)) : Subgroup (FreeGroup ℕ) :=
  Subgroup.closure {w | ∃ s ∈ S, ∃ φ : FreeGroup ℕ →* FreeGroup ℕ, φ s = w}
blocks.docstring:
The verbal subgroup of `FreeGroup ℕ` determined by a set of words `S`: the subgroup
generated by all images of elements of `S` under endomorphisms of `FreeGroup ℕ`. Its
elements are exactly the consequences of the words in `S`, i.e. the words that are
identities of every group in which all words of `S` are identities.

justification.closest_existing_considered: Subgroup.closure / Subgroup.normalClosure (not endomorphism-closed, so insufficient on their own); Mathlib has no verbal/fully invariant subgroup notion.
justification.name: Kourovka.«1.87».verbalSubgroup
justification.why_needed: The verbal subgroup of FreeGroup ℕ determined by a set of words S: Subgroup.closure of all images of elements of S under endomorphisms of FreeGroup ℕ. Its elements are exactly the consequences of S (the smallest fully invariant subgroup containing S; it is automatically normal since conjugations are endomorphisms). Needed to express 'every law of G is a consequence of the finite set S'. Tests: subset_verbalSubgroup, verbalSubgroup_empty, verbalSubgroup_of_zero.

def HasFiniteBasisOfLaws (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∃ S : Finset (FreeGroup ℕ), verbalSubgroup ↑S = laws G
blocks.docstring:
A group `G` has a finite basis of identities if there is a finite set `S` of words
whose consequences are exactly the identities of `G`; equivalently, the variety of
groups generated by `G` is finitely based.

justification.closest_existing_considered: No notion of (finitely based) group variety exists in Mathlib or FormalConjecturesForMathlib.

justification.why_needed: 'G has a finite basis of identities': ∃ S : Finset (FreeGroup ℕ), verbalSubgroup ↑S = laws G. (The equation forces S ⊆ laws G, since S ⊆ verbalSubgroup S.) Test: hasFiniteBasisOfLaws_unit.

claims.decomposer_note: Back-reference to Kourovka 1.86 (Shmel'kin): 'Does every finitely generated soluble group have a finite basis of identities?', so the Prop is: for every field K, every n, and every (finitely generated, hypothesis inherited from 1.86) subgroup G of GL_n(K), the variety generated by G is finitely based, i.e. some finite set of laws of G (elements of FreeGroup ℕ killed by every hom into G) has as consequences all laws of G; yes/no question with no candidate answer asserted, to be stated as answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ ... ; Mathlib has no group-variety vocabulary, so laws/consequence must be defined in the file.
claims.reviewer_why: All eight candidates state this slot identically in shape (answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ (K : Type) [Field K] (n : ℕ) (G : Subgroup (GL (Fin n) K)), G.FG → finitely-based G) and all compile. c07's bespoke vocabulary is the most transparent and robust: laws G = ⨅ φ : FreeGroup ℕ →* G, φ.ker; consequences = the verbal subgroup generated by all endomorphic images of the basis (H. Neumann's textbook definition, universe-free, and equal to the normal/fully invariant closure since the image set is conjugation-closed); finite basis = ∃ S : Finset, verbalSubgroup S = laws G. The semantic-consequence candidates (c01–c04, c06, c08) are also correct but rely on a universe-restriction argument (H : Type) that the reader must supply; c05 is equivalent to c07 but uses Type u for K and has no API tests. c07 also has proven API/test lemmas for every bespoke definition, as CONTRIBUTING.md requests. Boundary cases checked: n = 0 gives the trivial group (finitely based by {x₀}); K : Type is lossless because a f.g. subgroup of GL_n(K) lies over the countable subfield generated by its entries; answer(True) is the positive answer.

decomposition_objections.text: None of substance. The table's reading (finitely generated inherited from 1.86; 'soluble' not inherited) is the most natural one and was followed. A minor alternative reading, 'finitely generated soluble matrix groups', would make 1.87 a strict special case of 1.86; the two readings differ only for finitely generated virtually-soluble non-soluble linear groups (Tits alternative), and the table's version was kept.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 1.87

by A. L. Shmel'kin

Problem 1.86 of the Kourovka Notebook (also by Shmel'kin) asks: does every finitely
generated soluble group have a finite basis of identities? Problem 1.87 asks
"the same question for matrix groups (at least over a field of characteristic $0$)":
does every finitely generated group of matrices over a field $K$, i.e. every finitely
generated subgroup of $\mathrm{GL}_n(K)$, have a finite basis of identities? The
proposer asks this at least when $K$ has characteristic $0$.

An identity (law) of a group $G$ is a word $w$ in the free group $F$ on countably many
variables $x_0, x_1, \dots$ such that $w$ evaluates to $1$ under every substitution of
elements of $G$ for the variables, i.e. $\varphi(w) = 1$ for every homomorphism
$\varphi \colon F \to G$. A word $w$ is a consequence of a set $S$ of words if $w$ lies
in the verbal subgroup of $F$ determined by $S$, that is, the subgroup of $F$ generated
by all images of elements of $S$ under endomorphisms of $F$ (the smallest fully
invariant subgroup of $F$ containing $S$). A finite basis of identities of $G$ is a
finite set $S$ of words whose consequences are exactly the identities of $G$;
equivalently, the variety of groups generated by $G$ is finitely based.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«1.87»

/-- The subgroup of identities (laws) of a group `G`: the words `w` in the free group
`FreeGroup ℕ` on countably many variables such that `φ w = 1` for every homomorphism
`φ : FreeGroup ℕ →* G`, i.e. `w` evaluates to `1` under every substitution of elements
of `G` for the variables. -/
def laws (G : Type*) [Group G] : Subgroup (FreeGroup ℕ) :=
  ⨅ φ : FreeGroup ℕ →* G, φ.ker

/-- A word `w` is a law of `G` if and only if it evaluates to `1` under every substitution
`f : ℕ → G` of elements of `G` for the variables. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem mem_laws_iff {G : Type*} [Group G] {w : FreeGroup ℕ} :
    w ∈ laws G ↔ ∀ f : ℕ → G, FreeGroup.lift f w = 1 := by
  simp only [laws, Subgroup.mem_iInf, MonoidHom.mem_ker]
  exact ⟨fun h f => h (FreeGroup.lift f),
    fun h φ => by simpa using h (FreeGroup.lift.symm φ)⟩

/-- The trivial group satisfies every identity. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem laws_unit : laws Unit = ⊤ :=
  eq_top_iff.2 fun _ _ => mem_laws_iff.2 fun _ => Subsingleton.elim _ _

/-- The free group on countably many generators satisfies no non-trivial identity. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem laws_freeGroup : laws (FreeGroup ℕ) = ⊥ :=
  eq_bot_iff.2 fun w hw => by
    simpa [FreeGroup.lift_of_apply] using mem_laws_iff.1 hw FreeGroup.of

/-- The verbal subgroup of `FreeGroup ℕ` determined by a set of words `S`: the subgroup
generated by all images of elements of `S` under endomorphisms of `FreeGroup ℕ`. Its
elements are exactly the consequences of the words in `S`, i.e. the words that are
identities of every group in which all words of `S` are identities. -/
def verbalSubgroup (S : Set (FreeGroup ℕ)) : Subgroup (FreeGroup ℕ) :=
  Subgroup.closure {w | ∃ s ∈ S, ∃ φ : FreeGroup ℕ →* FreeGroup ℕ, φ s = w}

/-- Every word in `S` is a consequence of `S`. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem subset_verbalSubgroup (S : Set (FreeGroup ℕ)) : S ⊆ verbalSubgroup S :=
  fun s hs => Subgroup.subset_closure ⟨s, hs, MonoidHom.id _, rfl⟩

/-- The empty set of words has no non-trivial consequences. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem verbalSubgroup_empty : verbalSubgroup ∅ = ⊥ := by
  simp [verbalSubgroup]

/-- Every word is a consequence of the identity `x_0 = 1`. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem verbalSubgroup_of_zero : verbalSubgroup {FreeGroup.of 0} = ⊤ :=
  eq_top_iff.2 fun w _ =>
    Subgroup.subset_closure ⟨FreeGroup.of 0, rfl, FreeGroup.lift fun _ => w, by simp⟩

/-- A group `G` has a finite basis of identities if there is a finite set `S` of words
whose consequences are exactly the identities of `G`; equivalently, the variety of
groups generated by `G` is finitely based. -/
def HasFiniteBasisOfLaws (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∃ S : Finset (FreeGroup ℕ), verbalSubgroup ↑S = laws G

/-- The trivial group has a finite basis of identities, namely `{x_0}`. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem hasFiniteBasisOfLaws_unit : HasFiniteBasisOfLaws Unit :=
  ⟨{FreeGroup.of 0}, by rw [laws_unit, Finset.coe_singleton, verbalSubgroup_of_zero]⟩

/--
Does every finitely generated matrix group, i.e. every finitely generated subgroup $G$ of
$\mathrm{GL}_n(K)$ for a field $K$ and $n \geq 0$, have a finite basis of identities?

This is "the same question" as Problem 1.86 (does every finitely generated soluble group
have a finite basis of identities?) asked for matrix groups; the finite generation
hypothesis is carried over from Problem 1.86.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«1.87» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (K : Type) [Field K] (n : ℕ) (G : Subgroup (GL (Fin n) K)),
      G.FG → HasFiniteBasisOfLaws G := by
  sorry

/--
Does every finitely generated matrix group over a field of characteristic $0$, i.e. every
finitely generated subgroup $G$ of $\mathrm{GL}_n(K)$ for a field $K$ of characteristic
$0$ and $n \geq 0$, have a finite basis of identities?

This is the special case of Problem 1.87 that the proposer asks for "at least".
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«1.87».variants.char_zero : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (K : Type) [Field K] [CharZero K] (n : ℕ) (G : Subgroup (GL (Fin n) K)),
      G.FG → HasFiniteBasisOfLaws G := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«1.87»

items: 'Matrix group' is taken to mean a subgroup of GL_n(K) for a field K and some n : ℕ (n = 0 is harmless: the trivial group has the finite basis {x_0}).

The finite-generation hypothesis (G.FG) is carried over from Problem 1.86, as the decomposition table prescribes; the word 'soluble' is NOT carried over (the class 'matrix groups' replaces 'soluble groups'). By the Tits alternative this is essentially harmless: a f.g. linear group either contains a nonabelian free subgroup (then laws G = ⊥, finitely based by ∅) or is virtually soluble; so the only difference from a 'f.g. soluble matrix group' reading is the virtually-soluble non-soluble case. A reviewer may want to confirm this reading of 'the same question'.

Fields are quantified over Type (universe 0), following the repository idiom (cf. Kourovka/1_40.lean). This is WLOG: a finitely generated subgroup of GL_n(K) lies in GL_n(K₀) for the countable subfield K₀ generated by the entries of its generators.

Identities are words in FreeGroup ℕ (countably many variables x_0, x_1, …), the standard setting; 'consequence' is taken syntactically (membership in the verbal subgroup generated by S), which by Birkhoff's theorem coincides with the semantic notion (holds in every group satisfying S).
Characteristic 0 is expressed as [CharZero K], which for a field is equivalent to characteristic 0.

The bespoke definitions are kept in the problem file (as the task requires writing to a single path) rather than in FormalConjecturesForMathlib; they are generic enough that a reviewer might prefer to move them there.

reviewer_notes: Reading follows the decomposition table: 'the same question' as Kourovka 1.86 ('Does every finitely generated soluble group have a finite basis of identities?') with 'soluble group' replaced by 'matrix group' = subgroup of GL_n(K), K a field; the 'finitely generated' hypothesis is inherited (G.FG) and 'soluble' is not. Two residual interpretive points a human may want to confirm against the notebook: (1) whether 'finitely generated' is indeed meant to carry over (all candidates and the table assume so; without it the question would concern arbitrary linear groups), and (2) 'matrix groups' is taken over fields only, not over general commutative rings. Mathlib has no group-variety vocabulary, so laws/verbal subgroup/finite basis are defined in the problem file with proven test lemmas; they are generic enough that a maintainer might prefer moving them to FormalConjecturesForMathlib. The final file is c07's candidate.lean verbatim; it compiles with only 'declaration uses sorry' warnings.
